explanations: The defect is the floor division in allocate(). Each share is computed as total_cents * w // total_weight, and the remainder is never handed out. For a 100-cent refund over lines of 333, 333 and 334 cents, every share is 33, so the shares sum to 99. refund_order then credits cash_clearing with sum(shares), so the ledger is internally balanced and the LedgerImbalance check never fires. But the gateway was asked to refund 100 and orders.refunded_cents grows by 100, so the ledger records one cent less revenue reversal than actually left the business. The error is a few cents per refund and is invisible to the balance check; it only shows up in reconciliation against the payment processor. The fix is to distribute the leftover cents (largest remainder) so the shares always sum to total_cents.

Choice 4 is wrong because the early return happens before the UPDATE, so refunded_cents is not touched.

Correct: both writes share one database transaction, and an exception (including the rowcount check or an IntegrityError on a duplicate ref) rolls both back.
